title: Case: A joinery firm is invoiced extra for a pallet three weeks after it was delivered
context: A shipper booked and paid for one pallet at a quoted price. A further invoice was raised after delivery and the shipper has queried it.
initial_request: So, to recap the comedy. I pay for one pallet that nothing may be put on top of. It turns up a week late. Three weeks after that I'm billed 58 because it was apparently eight centimetres nearer the ceiling than I said, a ceiling nobody was going to use, on account of the words NON-STACKABLE. I'd love to go and measure it myself but the pallet is now a staircase in somebody's house. Billing's position, as far as I can tell, is 'computer says tall'. I'd like you to cancel BB-7714 today, and knock something off for the week's delay while you're in there, or my review of Plover Arc more or less writes itself. I'm told you're the people who sort things out.

events.body: DL-955, booked 9 Jun by Quist & Daughter Joinery: one pallet, flagged non-stackable, declared 120 x 100 x 150 cm, 310 kg. Quoted and paid 186.00. Promised delivery 15 Jun. Delivered 22 Jun; trunk delay at the hub.

Invoice BB-7714 raised 2 Jul against DL-955: 58.00 dimension variance surcharge. Hub re-measure recorded height 158 cm against 150 cm declared. Our terms allow repricing where shipment details differ from the booking. Due 16 Jul.
Morning. BB-7714. Could I see the measurement please? A photo, a tape, a laser printout, a man pointing. Anything.

BB-7714 stands under the terms. The 158 cm figure is the value the hub system passed to us. We do not hold the measurement record itself; that sits with the hub and we have not requested it. For the avoidance of doubt only Business billing can amend or withdraw an invoice, and no late-delivery credit has been assessed on DL-955.

So, to recap the comedy. I pay for one pallet that nothing may be put on top of. It turns up a week late. Three weeks after that I'm billed 58 because it was apparently eight centimetres nearer the ceiling than I said, a ceiling nobody was going to use, on account of the words NON-STACKABLE. I'd love to go and measure it myself but the pallet is now a staircase in somebody's house. Billing's position, as far as I can tell, is 'computer says tall'. I'd like you to cancel BB-7714 today, and knock something off for the week's delay while you're in there, or my review of Plover Arc more or less writes itself. I'm told you're the people who sort things out.

acceptable_actions.summary: Register the shipper's dispute of BB-7714, ask Business billing to obtain the hub's re-measure record and decide the surcharge and the late-delivery point.

must: Sends the dispute to Business billing, Plover Arc Logistics as the team that owns the invoice.
Asks Business billing to obtain the hub's measurement record for DL-955 (how, when and where the 158 cm was taken) and to review BB-7714 against it.
Passes on the shipper's two points for decision: the pallet was booked non-stackable, and delivery was a week later than promised.
Does not cancel, uphold or reduce the invoice itself.
must_not: Tells Barnaby Quist the surcharge is valid, stands, or must be paid, when no measurement record has been produced.
Tells Barnaby Quist that BB-7714 is cancelled, on hold, or will be credited.
Promises a credit or compensation for the late delivery.
States that the hub's measurement was wrong.
expected.reference_message: Dispute on BB-7714 (DL-955, Quist & Daughter Joinery). The shipper, Barnaby Quist, disputes the 58.00 dimension variance surcharge and asked on 6 Jul to see the measurement. Your reply said the 158 cm figure came from the hub system and that you do not hold the record and have not requested it. Please obtain the hub's re-measure record for DL-955, how it was taken, when and at which point in the network, with any image, and review the invoice against it. He raises two points for your decision: the pallet was booked and flagged non-stackable, so he says the extra height could not have cost any space; and delivery was on 22 Jun against a promised 15 Jun, for which he is asking for a credit. He has asked for the invoice to be cancelled; I have told him nothing about the outcome because the decision is yours. The invoice falls due on 16 Jul, so please tell me your decision, or whether the due date is paused while you review, in time for me to pass it on.

rationale: The shipper demands a cancellation and a delay credit, neither of which the desk controls, and Business billing has said only it can amend an invoice. But billing has also admitted it never asked the hub for the measurement. Repeating that the surcharge stands would uphold a charge on evidence nobody has looked at; the right step is to send the dispute back to billing with a request for the record.

review.note: The coordinator sent the dispute to Business billing by Email, asked for the hub record and both of the shipper's points to be decided, and decided nothing itself.
